examples.ko: 그 가게는 간판이 볼품없이 낡아서 처음엔 그냥 지나쳤어요.
examples.en: The shop's sign was so shabbily worn that I walked right past it at first.

examples.ko: 비를 맞아서 머리가 볼품없이 젖어 버렸어요.
examples.en: I got caught in the rain and my hair got soaked and looked a mess.

examples.ko: 선물이 볼품없이 포장돼 있었지만 안에는 좋은 게 들어 있었어요.
examples.en: The gift was wrapped plainly, but there was something nice inside.

examples.ko: 그 화분은 겨울을 지나면서 볼품없이 말라 갔어요.
examples.en: That plant dried up and looked sorry as winter went by.

examples.ko: 처음 만든 케이크가 볼품없이 무너져 버렸어요.
examples.en: The first cake I made collapsed into a sad-looking heap.

examples.ko: 작은 마당이 볼품없이 비어 있어서 꽃을 심기로 했어요.
examples.en: The small yard looked bare and dull, so I decided to plant flowers.

explain: '볼품없다'에서 나온 부사예요. 낡거나 초라해서 보기 좋지 않은 모습에 써요. 사람의 겉모습에 쓰면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있으니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is the adverb form of '볼품없다'. Use it for things that look old, plain or shabby. Be careful about using it for a person's appearance, because it can sound hurtful.

examples.ko: 주말에 가족과 함께 봄맞이 대청소를 했어요.
examples.en: On the weekend, my family and I did a big spring cleaning.

examples.ko: 백화점에서 이번 주부터 봄맞이 세일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The department store started its spring sale this week.

examples.ko: 봄맞이 옷을 사러 친구와 시장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the market with a friend to buy clothes for spring.
A spring welcoming festival is held in our neighborhood.
To welcome spring, I changed the living room curtains.

examples.ko: 봄맞이 준비로 베란다 화분에 꽃을 심었어요.
examples.en: To get ready for spring, I planted flowers in the pots on the balcony.

explain: '봄맞이 대청소', '봄맞이 세일'처럼 뒤에 다른 명사를 붙여서 자주 써요. '새해맞이', '손님맞이'처럼 '-맞이'가 붙은 말이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It is often followed by another noun, as in '봄맞이 대청소' (spring cleaning) or '봄맞이 세일' (spring sale). There are other words ending in '-맞이', such as '새해맞이' and '손님맞이'.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 봉고차를 타고 여행을 갔어요.
examples.en: My family took a van on our trip.
I loaded the van full of luggage.
My father sells fruit from a van.
The academy's van came to pick up the kids.

examples.ko: 봉고차는 자리가 넓어서 여러 명이 타기 좋아요.
examples.en: A van has lots of room, so it is good for carrying many people.
A friend borrowed a van and helped me move.

explain: 원래 한 회사의 차 이름에서 나온 말이지만 지금은 사람과 짐을 함께 싣는 큰 차를 두루 가리켜요. 공식적인 글이나 서류에서는 '승합차'라고 해요.
explain_en: It started as the name of one company's vehicle, but now people use it for any large van that carries both people and cargo. In formal writing and documents, the word is '승합차'.

examples.en: A service charge is added separately on the bill.
This restaurant does not charge a service fee.
This price includes a 10 percent service charge.
Do I have to pay the service charge separately at a hotel?
With the service charge added, it comes to more than I expected.
I checked the bill to see how much the service charge was.

explain: 호텔이나 고급 식당 계산서에 따로 적혀 있는 서비스 요금이에요. '서비스 요금'이라고도 해요. 한국은 팁 문화가 거의 없어서, 이 돈이 팁 대신이라고 생각하면 돼요.
explain_en: It is the service fee written as a separate line on bills at hotels and upscale restaurants. People also say '서비스 요금'. Tipping is not a common custom in Korea, so you can think of this as taking the place of a tip.

examples.en: The rosebuds are slowly opening.
Buds have formed all over the branches of the cherry tree.

examples.ko: 봉오리가 터지면 곧 꽃이 활짝 필 거예요.
examples.en: Once the buds burst, the flowers will bloom wide soon.
It is still a bud, but it already smells nice.
A single small bud bloomed by the window.

examples.ko: 봄비를 맞은 봉오리가 눈에 띄게 커졌어요.
examples.en: The buds that got the spring rain have grown noticeably bigger.

explain: 보통 '꽃봉오리'라는 말로 많이 써요. '꽃망울'도 비슷한 말이에요. '봉오리가 맺히다', '봉오리가 터지다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: People usually say '꽃봉오리' (flower bud). '꽃망울' is a similar word. It goes with set verbs, such as '봉오리가 맺히다' (buds form) and '봉오리가 터지다' (buds burst).

en: share of cost; cost to be borne

examples.en: How much of the hospital bill is my own share?
The landlord agreed to pay the repair costs.
I asked whether I could pay my share in installments.

examples.ko: 이번 모임 부담금은 한 사람당 오천 원이에요.
examples.en: The cost share for this gathering is 5,000 won per person.
Thanks to insurance, the amount I had to pay dropped a lot.
Don't miss the date for paying your share.

explain: 병원, 보험, 행사처럼 내가 맡아서 내야 하는 몫을 말할 때 써요. '본인 부담금'이라는 형태로 특히 자주 나와요. 정기적으로 내는 돈은 '회비'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: Use it for the share you have to pay for things like medical care, insurance or events. It appears very often as '본인 부담금' (the patient's or your own share). Money paid regularly to a group is called '회비' (membership fee), which is a different thing.

examples.en: In the evening I took a walk along the quay.

examples.ko: 부둣가에 작은 배들이 줄지어 서 있어요.
examples.en: Small boats are lined up along the wharf.
I ate fresh raw fish at a restaurant by the harbor.
A friend and I sat by the pier and watched the sunset.
The wharf is crowded with people from dawn.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 할아버지 댁이 부둣가 근처에 있었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, my grandfather's house was near the wharf.

explain: '부두'의 가장자리, 즉 배를 대는 곳 바로 옆을 말해요. '항구'는 도시나 지역 전체를, '부두'는 배를 대는 시설을 가리켜서 좀 달라요. 쓸 때는 '부둣가에서', '부둣가를 따라'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means the area right beside a '부두' (wharf), where ships dock. '항구' (port) refers to the whole harbor town or area, while '부두' is the docking facility. You will hear it as '부둣가에서' or '부둣가를 따라'.

examples.en: The child cries and clings to its mother.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 서로 부둥켜안고 한참 울었어요.
examples.en: The two of them held each other tight and cried for a long time.
I hugged my friend tightly and rejoiced at seeing them after so long.
The baby fell asleep hugging a doll.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 온 가족이 서로 부둥켜안았어요.
examples.en: At the news that I passed, the whole family hugged one another.

examples.ko: 힘들 때 누가 부둥켜안아 주면 위로가 돼요.
examples.en: When things are hard, it is comforting if someone gives you a big hug.

explain: '안다'보다 훨씬 힘을 주어 꽉 안는 느낌이에요. 반가움이나 슬픔 같은 큰 감정이 있을 때 많이 써요. '껴안다'는 더 평범하게 안는 말이고, '부둥켜안다'는 인형이나 짐 같은 물건을 꼭 붙잡을 때도 써요.
explain_en: It feels much stronger than '안다', as if you hold on with real force. It is often used when emotions run high, such as joy or sorrow. '껴안다' is the plainer word for hugging, while '부둥켜안다' can also be used when you clutch an object like a doll or a bag.

examples.en: I'm so cold that my body is trembling.

examples.ko: 너무 화가 나서 손이 부들부들 떨렸어요.
examples.en: I was so angry that my hands were shaking.

examples.ko: 발표 전에 다리가 부들부들 떨려서 혼났어요.
examples.en: My legs were shaking before the presentation and I had a hard time.
The child was scared and spoke with a trembling voice.
The hand holding the coffee cup is quivering.

examples.ko: 그는 겁이 나서 부들부들 떨기만 했어요.
examples.en: He was frightened and could only tremble.

explain: 추위, 두려움, 화, 힘든 일 때문에 몸이 계속 떨리는 모양이에요. 거의 항상 '떨다'와 함께 써요. '덜덜', '벌벌'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes the body shaking continuously from cold, fear, anger or strain. It almost always goes with the verb '떨다'. '덜덜' and '벌벌' are used in similar ways.

examples.en: The cold wind blew and I shivered.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 그가 부르르 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: Hearing that, he suddenly flared up in anger.
My phone buzzed, so I opened my bag.
The water for the ramen is bubbling up.

examples.ko: 아이가 차가운 물에 닿자 부르르 몸을 떨었어요.
examples.en: The child touched cold water and gave a shiver.
I suddenly got goosebumps and shuddered.

explain: 몸이 짧게 한 번 떨리거나 물건이 진동하는 모양, 물이 확 끓는 모양, 갑자기 성을 내는 모양에 써요. '부들부들'은 계속 떨리는 느낌이고 '부르르'는 짧고 갑작스러운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It covers a quick shiver of the body, something vibrating, water suddenly boiling up, and a sudden flare of temper. '부들부들' feels like trembling that keeps going, while '부르르' is short and sudden.

examples.en: Even between husband and wife, you should be polite.
Though they are husband and wife, they get along like friends.

examples.ko: 부부지간이라고 해서 모든 걸 말하지는 않아요.
examples.en: Just because they are married doesn't mean they tell each other everything.
My parents have a really good marriage.
Don't fight over things like this as a married couple.
Those two look after each other like a married couple.

explain: '부부 사이'라는 뜻으로, '부부지간에', '부부지간이라서'처럼 조사를 붙여 말해요. '부자지간', '모녀지간', '형제지간'처럼 '-지간'이 붙는 말이 여러 개 있어요. 대화에서는 그냥 '부부 사이'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: It means 'the relationship between spouses', and you attach particles to it, as in '부부지간에' or '부부지간이라서'. There are other words with '-지간', such as '부자지간', '모녀지간' and '형제지간'. In conversation people also often just say '부부 사이'.

examples.ko: 주말에 번역 일을 해서 부수입이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I did translation work on weekends and made some extra income.
Thanks to the side income, I saved up for the trip.
I wish I had some extra income besides my salary.
He earns a little side income from his blog.
I use the extra money to help with living expenses.

examples.ko: 용돈 벌이로 시작했는데 부수입이 꽤 커졌어요.
examples.en: It started as pocket money, but the side income has grown quite a bit.

explain: 본업의 월급 말고 따로 생기는 돈을 말해요. '부업'은 하는 일이고 '부수입'은 그 일로 번 돈이라서 달라요. '부수입이 생기다', '부수입을 올리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is money that comes in apart from your main salary. '부업' is the side job itself, while '부수입' is the money you earn from it. It is used in phrases like '부수입이 생기다' and '부수입을 올리다'.

examples.en: The snacks all crumbled inside my bag.
The old wall crumbles when I touch it with my hand.

examples.ko: 빵이 너무 말라서 먹을 때 부스러져요.
examples.en: The bread is so dry that it crumbles when I eat it.
Be careful, because the biscuit will crumble if you grip it hard.
The dry leaves crunched and crumbled when I stepped on them.
The cookie crumbled and the plate is full of crumbs.

explain: 딱딱하고 마른 것이 작은 조각이나 가루로 되는 모습이에요. 그 조각을 '부스러기'라고 해요. '부서지다'는 큰 물건이 깨질 때도 쓰지만, '부스러지다'는 과자나 낙엽처럼 잘게 되는 것에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes something hard and dry breaking into tiny pieces or powder. The pieces are called '부스러기' (crumbs). '부서지다' can also describe a big object breaking, while '부스러지다' suits things like biscuits and dry leaves that break into small bits.

examples.ko: 밤에 쥐가 부스럭거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: A mouse was rustling at night, so I couldn't sleep.
The person next to me keeps rustling a plastic bag.

examples.ko: 영화 중에 과자를 부스럭거리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't rustle snack bags during a movie.
I hear someone rustling around in the room.
The child rustled around under the blanket and then got up.
When I walk on fallen leaves, they rustle under my feet.

explain: 마른 종이, 비닐, 낙엽처럼 마른 것이 스치는 소리가 나거나 그런 소리를 내며 움직인다는 말이에요. '부스럭대다'도 같은 뜻이에요. '바스락거리다'는 조금 더 가볍고 작은 소리 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes the dry sound of things like paper, plastic or leaves rubbing together, or moving while making that sound. '부스럭대다' means the same thing. '바스락거리다' feels a little lighter and softer in sound.

examples.en: I woke up this morning and my hair is a mess.
On humid days my hair gets frizzy, which worries me.
He opened the door with a rumpled, just-woke-up face.
The perm came out and my hair got even messier.
My hair is messy, so I'll wear a hat.
The child's hair was tousled after waking up.

explain: 머리카락이나 털이 정돈되지 않고 일어나 있는 모습에 많이 써요. 자고 일어난 얼굴이나 푸석한 모습에도 쓰지만, 머리와 가장 잘 어울려요. '푸석푸석하다'는 윤기 없이 마른 느낌이 중심이에요.
explain_en: It is used mostly for hair or fur that is untidy and sticking up. It can also describe a rumpled, just-woke-up face, but it goes best with hair. '푸석푸석하다' focuses more on a dry, lusterless look.

examples.en: It has been drizzling since morning.

examples.ko: 부슬부슬 내리는 비 속을 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked slowly through the drizzling rain.

examples.ko: 가을 오후에 부슬부슬 비가 와서 기분이 차분해요.
examples.en: A light rain on an autumn afternoon makes me feel calm.

examples.ko: 부슬부슬 내리는 비라서 우산 없이 나왔어요.
examples.en: It was only a light drizzle, so I came out without an umbrella.

examples.ko: 부슬부슬 비가 오는 날에는 전이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On days when it drizzles, I want to eat jeon.
The drizzle that had been falling stopped in the evening.

explain: 가늘고 조용하게 내리는 비를 말할 때 써요. 센 비는 '주룩주룩'처럼 다른 말을 써요. '보슬보슬'도 비슷한데 더 부드럽고 작은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes thin, quiet rain. Heavy rain is described with other words such as '주룩주룩'. '보슬보슬' is similar but feels even softer and finer.

examples.ko: 부자지간인데도 둘은 서로 말이 거의 없어요.
examples.en: Even though they are father and son, they hardly talk to each other.

examples.ko: 저 둘은 부자지간이라서 얼굴이 정말 닮았어요.
examples.en: Those two are father and son, so their faces look really alike.

examples.ko: 부자지간에 함께 낚시를 가는 모습이 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: It is nice to see a father and son going fishing together.

examples.ko: 우리 아버지와 저는 부자지간이지만 친구처럼 지내요.
examples.en: My father and I are father and son, but we get along like friends.

examples.ko: 부자지간의 대화가 늘어서 집안 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The father and son talk more now, so the mood at home has improved.
At work they are boss and subordinate, but at home they are father and son.

explain: 아버지와 아들 사이를 말해요. 아버지와 딸은 '부녀지간', 어머니와 딸은 '모녀지간', 어머니와 아들은 '모자지간'처럼 '-지간' 앞의 말만 바꿔 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '아빠랑 아들 사이'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the relationship between a father and his son. You change the word before '-지간' for other pairs, such as '부녀지간' (father and daughter), '모녀지간' (mother and daughter) or '모자지간' (mother and son). In everyday talk people also say things like '아빠랑 아들 사이'.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 학교에서 부적응 문제를 겪고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is having trouble adjusting at the new school.

examples.ko: 학교 부적응 때문에 상담을 받기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to get counseling because of the difficulty adjusting to school.

examples.ko: 신입 사원의 부적응을 줄이려고 교육을 해요.
examples.en: They run training to reduce new employees' adjustment problems.
If the adjustment problem lasts long, you need an expert's help.
I have a friend who is struggling because he can't adjust to the military.

examples.ko: 부적응 증상이 나타나면 선생님과 이야기해 보세요.
examples.en: If signs of poor adjustment show up, talk with your teacher.

explain: 학교, 직장, 사회처럼 어떤 환경에 맞추어 살지 못하는 상태를 말해요. '학교 부적응', '사회 부적응'처럼 앞에 환경을 붙여 써요. 반대말은 '적응'이고, 그런 사람은 '부적응자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to being unable to fit in with an environment such as school, work or society. People attach the environment before it, as in '학교 부적응' or '사회 부적응'. The opposite is '적응', and a person in that state is a '부적응자'.

examples.ko: 시험 중 부정행위를 하면 영점 처리돼요.
examples.en: If you cheat during an exam, you get a zero.

examples.ko: 부정행위를 한 학생은 다시 시험을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: A student who cheated has to take the exam again.
The proctor checked the bags to prevent cheating.

examples.ko: 부정행위로 의심받을 만한 행동은 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't do anything that could be suspected as cheating.
Wrongdoing at the company came to light and was on the news.

examples.ko: 시험 중에 휴대폰을 보는 것도 부정행위가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even looking at your phone during an exam can count as cheating.

explain: 주로 시험이나 시합, 회사 일에서 규칙을 어기는 행동을 말해요. 시험에서는 일상 대화에서 '커닝'이라고 많이 하고, '부정행위'는 공식적인 말이에요. '부정행위를 하다', '부정행위가 적발되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for breaking the rules in exams, competitions or business. For exam cheating, people in daily talk often say '커닝', while '부정행위' is the formal word. It goes with '부정행위를 하다' (to cheat) and '부정행위가 적발되다' (to be caught cheating).

examples.en: I went to my friend's wedding and gave a monetary gift.
I don't know how much to give as a monetary gift.
I sent condolence money to my friend's father's funeral.

examples.ko: 부조금 봉투에 이름을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must write your name on the money envelope.
At work, we collected money from the staff separately as a gift.

examples.ko: 부조금은 축하나 위로하는 마음을 담아 내요.
examples.en: People give this money to express congratulations or comfort.

explain: 결혼식이나 장례식처럼 큰일이 있는 집에 돕는 마음으로 내는 돈이에요. 결혼식에는 '축의금', 장례식에는 '조의금'이라고 나누어 말하기도 해요. 보통 봉투에 넣어서 내요.
explain_en: It is money given to a family holding a big event, such as a wedding or funeral, as a way of helping out. People often distinguish '축의금' for weddings and '조의금' for funerals. It is usually handed over in an envelope.

examples.en: We learned how to find the area of a sector in math class.
A slice of pizza is shaped like a fan.
I folded paper and made a fan shape.
The problem of finding the central angle of a sector was hard.
The peacock spread its tail wide like a fan.

examples.ko: 이 공원의 무대는 부채꼴로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The stage in this park is fan-shaped.

explain: 수학에서는 원의 일부인 도형을 가리키지만, 일상에서는 한쪽이 좁고 점점 넓어지는 모양을 비유로도 말해요. '부채 모양'이라고도 해요. '-꼴'은 모양을 나타내요.
explain_en: In math it names a shape that is part of a circle (a sector), but in daily life it also describes any shape that starts narrow and widens out. You can also say '부채 모양'. The '-꼴' part means 'shape'.

examples.en: It was hot, so I fanned myself with my hand.
My grandmother fanned me from the side.
I fanned the charcoal to get the fire going.

examples.ko: 여름밤에 마루에 앉아 부채질하며 수박을 먹었어요.
examples.en: On a summer night I sat on the porch, fanning myself and eating watermelon.
His face turned red and he keeps fanning himself.
After fanning myself, I felt a little cooler.

explain: 꼭 부채가 아니어도 손이나 종이로 바람을 일으키면 '부채질하다'라고 해요. 선풍기 바람을 쐬는 것은 이렇게 말하지 않아요. 비유로 어떤 감정이나 싸움을 더 키운다는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 화난 친구에게 그런 말을 하면 불난 집에 부채질하는 거예요.
phrases.en: Saying that to an angry friend is adding fuel to the fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안 좋은 상황이나 화난 사람을 더 나쁘게 만드는 행동을 말해요. 보통 '불난 집에 부채질하다'라는 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes making a bad situation or an angry person even worse. It is almost always used in the full form '불난 집에 부채질하다'.

explain_en: You do not need an actual fan; waving your hand or a piece of paper to make a breeze counts as '부채질하다'. You would not use it for sitting in front of an electric fan. It is also used figuratively for making a feeling or a fight worse.

examples.ko: 부처님 오신 날에 가족과 절에 갔어요.
examples.en: On Buddha's Birthday I went to a temple with my family.
My grandmother prays to Buddha every morning.

examples.ko: 절 법당에 큰 부처님이 앉아 계세요.
examples.en: A large Buddha statue is seated in the temple hall.

examples.ko: 부처님 앞에서 두 손을 모으고 인사했어요.
examples.en: I put my hands together and bowed before the Buddha.

examples.ko: 사월 초파일에는 부처님을 기리는 행사가 열려요.
examples.en: On the eighth day of the fourth lunar month, events honoring Buddha are held.

examples.ko: 그분은 부처님처럼 마음이 넓다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: People say that person has a heart as wide as Buddha's.

explain: '부처'를 높여 부르는 말이라서 '부처님께'처럼 높임 조사를 써요. 절에 있는 불상을 가리킬 때도, 부처 그분을 말할 때도 써요. '불상'은 조각이나 그림으로 된 모습만 가리켜서 좀 달라요.

phrases.example: 그 선생님은 부처님 가운데 토막 같은 분이라 화내는 걸 본 적이 없어요.
phrases.en: That teacher is as gentle as a saint; I have never seen them get angry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음씨가 아주 착하고 너그러운 사람을 칭찬할 때 '부처님 가운데 토막 같다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: You use '부처님 가운데 토막 같다' to praise a person who is extremely kind and generous.

explain_en: It is the respectful form of '부처' (Buddha), so you use honorific particles, as in '부처님께'. It can mean the Buddha statue in a temple or the Buddha himself. '불상' refers only to the statue or image, so it is narrower.

examples.en: I packed butane gas when I went camping.

examples.ko: 부탄가스가 떨어져서 불을 켤 수 없어요.
examples.en: The butane ran out, so I can't light the stove.
I put a butane canister into the portable gas stove.
Butane canisters are dangerous if kept close to a fire.
I bought four cans of butane at the supermarket.

examples.ko: 다 쓴 부탄가스는 분리배출 안내를 보고 버리세요.
examples.en: Check the recycling instructions before throwing away empty butane cans.

explain: 캠핑이나 집에서 휴대용 가스레인지에 끼워 쓰는 작은 통을 보통 이렇게 불러요. '부탄가스 한 통'처럼 '통'으로 세요. 열이나 불 근처에서는 위험하니까 보관할 때 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: People usually use this name for the small canister that fits into a portable gas stove, whether camping or at home. You count them with '통', as in '부탄가스 한 통'. They are dangerous near heat or fire, so storage needs care.

examples.en: I found the Big Dipper in the clear night sky.
The Big Dipper is shaped like a ladle.

examples.ko: 아빠가 북두칠성으로 북극성 찾는 법을 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: My dad showed me how to find the North Star using the Big Dipper.
In the countryside, the Big Dipper is clearly visible.

examples.ko: 북두칠성의 일곱 별을 하나씩 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: I counted the seven stars of the Big Dipper one by one.
It is hard to see the Big Dipper in the city.

explain: 국자 모양으로 늘어선 일곱 별이에요. 국자 끝의 두 별을 이어 길게 늘이면 북극성을 찾을 수 있어요. 전통적으로 수명을 맡은 별로 여겨서, 관 바닥에 까는 '칠성판'에도 일곱 별 모양으로 구멍을 냈어요. 줄여서 '칠성'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the seven stars arranged in the shape of a ladle. If you extend a line through the two stars at the end of the ladle, you can find the North Star. Traditionally the stars were believed to govern lifespan, and the board laid at the bottom of a coffin, the '칠성판', is bored with holes in the shape of the seven stars. It is sometimes shortened to '칠성'.

examples.en: Korea is in the Northern Hemisphere.
When it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere, it is winter in the Southern Hemisphere.

examples.ko: 북반구에서는 칠월이 가장 더운 달 중 하나예요.
examples.en: In the Northern Hemisphere, July is one of the hottest months.

examples.ko: 이 철새는 가을마다 북반구에서 남쪽으로 이동해요.
examples.en: This migratory bird moves south from the Northern Hemisphere every autumn.
The Northern and Southern Hemispheres have opposite seasons.
We are in the Northern Hemisphere, so Christmas is in winter.

explain: 적도를 기준으로 북쪽 절반을 말하고 반대말은 '남반구'예요. 한국, 미국, 유럽이 북반구에 있어요. 북반구가 여름이면 남반구는 겨울이라서 호주에서는 크리스마스가 한여름이에요.
explain_en: It means the northern half of the Earth, divided at the equator, and its opposite is '남반구'. Korea, the United States and Europe are all in the Northern Hemisphere. When it is summer in the north it is winter in the south, so Christmas falls in midsummer in Australia.

examples.en: I bought one dried pollack at the market.
I soaked the dried pollack in water and made soup.

examples.ko: 새 차를 사면 북어를 달아 두는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people hang dried pollack in a new car.
I pounded the dried pollack with a mallet to soften it.
Mom is peeling the skin off the dried pollack.

examples.ko: 북어는 오래 보관할 수 있어서 집에 늘 있어요.
examples.en: Dried pollack keeps for a long time, so we always have some at home.

explain: 같은 명태라도 상태에 따라 이름이 달라요. 얼리면 '동태', 겨울에 얼렸다 말리면 '황태', 그냥 바싹 말린 것은 '북어'라고 해요. 딱딱해서 방망이로 두드려 부드럽게 한 뒤에 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: The same pollack gets different names depending on how it is treated: frozen is '동태', freeze-dried over winter is '황태', and simply dried hard is '북어'. It is so stiff that people often pound it with a mallet to soften it before cooking.

examples.ko: 속이 안 좋을 때는 북엇국이 최고예요.
examples.en: When your stomach feels bad, bugeoguk is the best.
I beat an egg and stirred it into the dried pollack soup.
I ordered the dried pollack soup set meal at the restaurant.
For breakfast I had warm dried pollack soup and rice.
Bugeoguk is popular because the broth is refreshing.
The bugeoguk my mom makes is the tastiest.

explain: 북어를 넣고 끓인 맑고 시원한 국이에요. 속이 불편할 때 찾는 사람이 많아요. 달걀을 풀거나 두부, 무를 넣어서 끓이는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a clear, refreshing soup made with dried pollack. Many people reach for it when their stomach feels uneasy. It is often cooked with beaten egg, tofu or radish.

examples.en: It's the weekend, so the market is bustling with people.

examples.ko: 명절에는 기차역이 늘 북적대서 표 구하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The train station is always crowded during holidays, so it is hard to get tickets.

examples.ko: 식당 앞이 줄 선 사람들로 북적대고 있어요.
examples.en: The area in front of the restaurant is crowded with people in line.
The bustling noise from next door woke me up.
The library is not crowded on weekday afternoons.
It's a holiday, so what do we do if the airport is packed?

explain: 사람이 많이 모여서 복잡하고 시끌시끌한 모습이에요. '북적거리다'도 같은 뜻이에요. '붐비다'는 사람이 많아 복잡하다는 점이 중심이고, '북적대다'는 활기나 소란스러운 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a place full of people, busy and noisy. '북적거리다' means the same thing. '붐비다' focuses on being crowded, while '북적대다' also carries a feeling of liveliness or noise.

examples.en: A cold north wind blows in winter.
The north wind is blowing hard and my hands are freezing.
I walked to school facing the north wind.

examples.ko: 오늘은 북풍 때문에 체감 온도가 더 낮아요.
examples.en: Because of the north wind, it feels colder today.

examples.ko: 북풍이 부는 날에는 목도리를 꼭 해요.
examples.en: I always wear a scarf on days when the north wind blows.
A north wind suddenly gusted and the windows rattled.

explain: 북쪽에서 불어오는 바람이에요. 한국에서는 겨울의 차갑고 센 바람을 떠올리게 해요. 반대로 남쪽에서 불어오는 바람은 '남풍'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the wind that blows from the north. In Korea it brings to mind the cold, strong winds of winter. The wind from the south is called '남풍'.

examples.en: The pot got too small, so I repotted the plant.

examples.ko: 봄에 분갈이를 하면 식물이 잘 자라요.
examples.en: If you repot in spring, plants grow well.

examples.ko: 분갈이할 때 새 흙을 사야 해요.
examples.en: You need to buy new soil when repotting.
The roots are poking out, so it looks like it needs repotting.

examples.ko: 주말에 베란다에서 분갈이를 했더니 손이 엉망이에요.
examples.en: I repotted on the balcony over the weekend and my hands are a mess.

examples.ko: 분갈이를 한 뒤에는 물을 충분히 주세요.
examples.en: After repotting, give it plenty of water.

explain: 화분 속 식물을 더 큰 화분이나 새 흙으로 옮겨 심는 일이에요. 보통 '분갈이를 하다'라고 말하고 '분갈이하다'로도 써요. 식물을 키우는 사람들이 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the job of moving a potted plant into a bigger pot or fresh soil. You usually say '분갈이를 하다', and '분갈이하다' also works. It is a word plant keepers use all the time.

examples.en: Korea has existed as a divided country for a long time.

examples.ko: 분단국가에 사는 사람들은 통일에 관심이 많아요.
examples.en: People living in a divided country are very interested in reunification.
In history class we learned about examples of divided countries.
Germany was also once a divided country.
The fact that it is a divided country is often mentioned in the news.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구가 분단국가에서의 생활이 궁금하다고 했어요.
examples.en: A foreign friend said they were curious about life in a divided country.

explain: 한 나라가 정치적인 이유로 둘 이상으로 나뉜 상태의 나라를 말해요. 한국 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 짝이 되는 말은 '통일'이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a country split into two or more parts for political reasons. It comes up often when talking about Korea. Its counterpart is '통일' (unification).

examples.en: If the denominators are the same, you just add the numerators.
I found a common denominator for the two fractions.
I learned that the denominator cannot be zero.

examples.ko: 선생님이 분모와 분자를 헷갈리지 말라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us not to mix up the denominator and numerator.

examples.ko: 분자가 같을 때는 분모가 클수록 값이 작아요.
examples.en: When the numerators are the same, a bigger denominator means a smaller value.
In this problem you have to multiply the denominator by 3.

explain: 짝이 되는 말 '분자'와 함께 외워요. 분수를 읽을 때는 '삼분의 이'처럼 분모를 먼저 읽어요. 수학 말고도 '공통분모'라는 비유로 일상에서 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 두 사람의 공통분모는 음악을 좋아한다는 점이에요.
phrases.en: What the two of them have in common is that they love music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 다른 사람이나 의견 사이에 같은 점을 말할 때 비유로 써요. 보통 '공통분모를 찾다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for the shared point between different people or opinions. You often say '공통분모를 찾다'.

explain_en: Learn it together with its partner '분자' (numerator). When reading fractions aloud, you say the denominator first, as in '삼분의 이' (two thirds). Outside math, it is used figuratively in '공통분모'.

examples.en: I sprayed water on the plant with a spray bottle.
Please fill the spray bottle with water.

examples.ko: 분무기가 고장 나서 물이 나오지 않아요.
examples.en: The sprayer is broken and no water comes out.

examples.ko: 머리가 뻗쳐서 분무기로 물을 살짝 뿌렸어요.
examples.en: My hair was sticking up, so I lightly misted it with water.
Using a spray bottle is handy when ironing.
I bought a new sprayer and left it on the balcony.

explain: 물이나 액체를 안개처럼 가늘게 뿜어 주는 도구예요. 화분에 물을 주는 '물뿌리개'는 물줄기가 나오는 점이 달라요. 일상에서는 '스프레이'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a tool that sprays water or liquid in a fine mist. A '물뿌리개' (watering can), used for watering plants, differs in that it pours out streams of water. In daily talk people also often say '스프레이'.
